clue.text: Strong winds spoil coast that's regularly eroded

parts.note: to spoil someone is to pamper or indulge them

indicators.note: regularly eroded means every other letter is worn away, leaving the alternate ones of coast

explanation.surface: A gale ruins a shoreline that is worn away at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly eroded' keeps the second and fourth letters of COAST, O and S. PAMPEROS are cold south-westerly winds blowing across the Argentine pampas.
explanation.definitionFit: Pamperos are fierce winds sweeping off the pampas of South America, so strong winds is a plain description.

clue.text: Warning about British taking a Canadian province

indicators.note: about means the warning word goes around the abbreviation for British

parts.note: an alert is a warning

explanation.surface: An alert goes out about Britain seizing a slice of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B inside ALERT to give ALBERT, and 'taking' then adds A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of the western prairie provinces of Canada, its capital Edmonton.

clue.text: Drinks fellow carried in posh travelling bag

indicators.note: carried in means the word for fellow sits inside the pair of drinks

parts.note: two drinks: port, the fortified wine, and tea
a fellow is a man
U stands for upper-class, hence posh, in crossword convention

explanation.surface: A chap's drinks are carried in a smart suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' supplies two drinks at once, one either side of the fellow. U meaning upper-class is an old British usage for posh.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large leather trunk that opens into two halves, a traditional bag for travel.

clue.text: Terrain no good for game of golf

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is taken away from the word for terrain

parts.note: terrain is ground, the land underfoot

explanation.surface: A golf course built on poor land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G (good) from GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A round of golf is one complete game played over the course's holes.

clue.text: Take a bit for the horse

definitions.meaning: to take something quickly or slyly, to nab or pinch it
a simple jointed mouthpiece put in a horse's mouth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to grab or pilfer and a light jointed bit used in riding.

clue.text: A new church leader from South America

parts.note: a dean is the head of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A freshly appointed cleric arrives from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean describes the Andes mountains and their peoples, which run the length of South America.

clue.text: Male is imprisoned in confined space for denying God

indicators.note: imprisoned in means the two pieces sit inside the word for a cramped room

parts.note: an attic is a cramped space under the roof
he is the male pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man is locked in a small room for rejecting religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male' looks like a description of the prisoner but simply gives the male pronoun; the attic is the cramped room under a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheistic outlook rejects belief in any deity, so it amounts to denying God.

clue.text: Creature made no mark in sleeping quarters

indicators.note: no means the letter for mark is dropped from the sleeping room

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
M is the abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency

explanation.surface: An animal leaves no trace in the dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes M (mark) from DORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dor is a dung beetle that drones as it flies, so a small creature.

clue.text: Seamen steered ship, say, to make quick getaway

parts.note: ABs are able seamen

indicators.note: say means the next word is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering, so steered ship is conned

explanation.surface: Sailors steered their vessel away in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you CONNED is heard as COND. To con a ship is a naval term for directing the helmsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to slip away secretly and fast, typically to escape justice.

clue.text: Pulled apart mother's absurd beachwear

indicators.note: pulled apart says the letters of the next words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A mother's ridiculous swimwear gets torn to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled apart' rearranges all the letters of MOTHERS ABSURD, the S of mother's included; 'absurd' is fodder, not a second signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermuda shorts are knee-length casual shorts worn on holiday and at the beach.

clue.text: Polluted sea east of Greek island

indicators.note: east of in an across clue means the sea word comes after the others

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A dirty sea lies to the east of a Greek isle.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'east of' means to the right, so the sea comes after the Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimed means coated with dirt or soot, which is what polluted means here.

clue.text: Shoe worn in summer or spring?

definitions.meaning: a light rubber sandal held by a thong between the toes
a spring here is a leap, a backward handspring in gymnastics

explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a thong sandal and a backward handspring, a gymnastic leap.

clue.text: Conventions supporting links with part of Africa

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
Mali is a country in West Africa
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: Customs backing connections with an African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Formalities are the customary procedures and conventions to be observed.

clue.text: Unusual way for dope to penetrate tropical region

indicators.note: to penetrate means the word for dope goes inside the word for unusual

parts.note: something rare is unusual
dope is slang for information, the info
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A strange route for drugs to enter the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope means information here, not drugs, and 'Unusual way' splits into two pieces rather than one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainforest is dense, wet forest found mostly in the tropics.

clue.text: Yo-yo is under one's control

definitions.meaning: a yo-yo hangs and spins on a cord

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a toy dangling on a cord and a person who is manipulated or dominated.

clue.text: You can hear roller coaster, perhaps, in IOW town

indicators.note: you can hear means the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a roller coaster is an example of a fairground ride

explanation.surface: Fairground screams can be heard in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast; RYDE is its largest town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryde is a seaside town on the north-east coast of the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: Keep wild dog

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the preceding word run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep an untamed hound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges KEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Peke is short for Pekingese, a small long-haired toy dog.

clue.text: Part of decor — cheesy stripped figure

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some tacky interior decoration featuring a naked figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecorche is an anatomical figure shown with the skin removed to display the muscles.

clue.text: Restored palace, then part of church

indicators.note: restored means the letters are rebuilt into a different order

explanation.surface: A palace is renovated and then becomes part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' rearranges PALACE THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An antechapel is the outer vestibule at the west end of a chapel.

clue.text: Artist's work wrapped up in fancy toile

indicators.note: in means the turned work sits inside the rearranged fabric word
fancy means the letters of toile are rearranged freely
wrapped up in a down clue means the work word is rolled upward, read from bottom to top

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A painter's work comes swathed in decorative fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Artist's' stands for 'is'. 'wrapped up' turns OP to PO in this down entry, 'fancy' makes TIELO from TOILE, and 'in' puts PO inside. Toile is a printed cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter famous for ceiling frescoes.

clue.text: Turn out as a member of soccer team

parts.note: to evert is to turn inside out
to be on a team or committee is to be a member of it

explanation.surface: Turning up to play for a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERTON is an English football club based in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club from Liverpool, so it is a soccer team.

clue.text: Fried food not right for sexy lady

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out of the fried food

parts.note: a croquette is a fried roll of mashed potato or meat in breadcrumbs

explanation.surface: Deep-fried snacks are unsuitable for an alluring woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R (right) from CROQUETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a flirtatious woman who toys with admirers, loosely a sexy lady.

clue.text: One looks happy with examinations over and pressure removed

indicators.note: removed means the letter for pressure is taken away
over means the exams word is turned back to front

parts.note: prelims are preliminary examinations
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone grins once the exams are done and stress has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PRELIMS into SMILERP, and 'removed' drops the P (pressure). PRELIMS are first-year university exams in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiler is a person wearing a smile, someone who appears happy.

clue.text: Boat visible when water's rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: pools are stretches of water

explanation.surface: A vessel comes into view as the tide comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns POOLS upward in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing boat with a fore-and-aft rig.

clue.text: Expert in the wrong

parts.note: seems to describe a specialist who has made a mistake, but reads as a specialist in wrongdoing, the study of crime

explanation.definitionFit: A criminologist is a scholar of crime, wrongdoing being the field of expertise.

clue.text: I study a language? That's unnatural

parts.note: to do a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone learning a language finds it artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: IDO is a constructed language derived from Esperanto, hence 'unnatural'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial auxiliary language devised in 1907, so it is a language that is not natural.

clue.text: Take ages to find a place?

definitions.meaning: split as two words this means to be slow
to have a proper place, to fit in somewhere

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to take a long time; as one it means to fit or have a rightful place.

clue.text: Disapproving of pop song I composed

indicators.note: composed means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Disliking a pop song I wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges POP SONG I.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing means being against something, hence disapproving of it.
